researcher_notes: Opus full-redo pass. SIXTEEN files collapsing to SEVEN processing units after md5 dedup (`eae-2a-…-specsheet` ×3 identical, `erc-2a-…-specsheet` ×2, `eks-215a-…-specsheet` ×2). Jungheinrich publishes a SPECSHEET + FACTSHEET pair per model: the specsheet carries the VDI 2198 Typenblatt and mast tables, the factsheet carries the marketing claims. Reading both halves is mandatory here — the specsheet's VDI battery row is a standard-configuration row that the factsheet routinely contradicts (documented on EKS 215a below), and the VDI disclaimer printed on every specsheet says so explicitly. `download-factsheet-amr-arculee-m-data.pdf` is a JUNGHEINRICH document despite the generic filename (p.2 heading 'Der kompakte und wendige Autonomous Mobile Robot arculee M', p.3 heading 'Jungheinrich arculee M'). Nothing written to Airtable.

company_wide_context.notes: MUST be fanned out per base model. THE LI-ION POINT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE and it is a worked example of false-positive check #3. The VDI Typenblatt on `eks-215a-2021-specsheet…pdf` p.5 gives row '6.3 Batterie nach DIN 43531/35/36: 5 PzS 775' and '6.4: 24 / 775 V/Ah' — i.e. LEAD-ACID — which contradicts the DB's `battery_type = Li-Ion` on that row. It is NOT a conflict: the companion `eks-215a-2021-factsheet…pdf` markets exactly the opposite, 'Das 24-V-Energiekonzept mit **Lithium-Ionen-Batterie** und Automatik-Ladefunktion' and 'Wirtschaftlicher 24/7-Betrieb dank Lithium-Ionen-Technologie'. Every specsheet in this group carries the disclaimer 'Dieses Typenblatt nach VDI-Richtlinie 2198 nennt nur die technischen Werte des Standard-Gerätes. Abweichende Bereifungen, andere Hubgerüste, Zusatzeinrichtungen usw. können andere Werte ergeben.' **Never flag a battery_type conflict from a Jungheinrich VDI row without reading the factsheet half.** The same applies to the ERC/ERE/EKX sheets, whose VDI rows also list PzS lead-acid. Certifications: every specsheet's back page states 'Zertifiziert sind die deutschen Produktionswerke in Norderstedt, Moosburg und Landsberg sowie unser Ersatzteilzentrum in Kaltenkirchen' and 'Jungheinrich Flurförderzeuge entsprechen den europäischen Sicherheitsanforderungen' — a certification claim with no standard named and a CE-equivalence statement. Not mapped: the existing company row already holds ISO 9001|ISO 14001|CE, which this neither confirms nor contradicts.

products.notes: NEW PRODUCT — Jungheinrich has no EAE row in the DB at all, and this is its newest Mobile Robot line (specsheet dated 08/2026, series introduced 2024). **`max_gradient = 0.0` is a REAL zero, not a missing value**, and the project's `Blank ≠ Zero` invariant makes the distinction load-bearing here: VDI row 5.7 prints '0 / 0 %' for automatic operation and the footnote gives '3 / 3 %' for manual. So this vehicle cannot handle ANY gradient under automation — a hard disqualifier for any site with a ramp, and precisely the kind of value that must not be confused with 'unknown'. If the import tooling cannot distinguish 0 from null on this field, it is better to leave it out and note it than to store a null. AP0 GAP: no aisle-width figure is published on this Typenblatt at all (no row 4.34), which for a low-lift transporter is a notable omission by the manufacturer rather than by AP0. `onboard_ui` NOT filled — the factsheet documents a real operator HMI ('Intelligente Kombination von Display und LED-Streifen am Fahrzeug', 'Klare Statusanzeige minimiert die Notwendigkeit manueller Eingriffe', factsheet p.3) but `onboard_ui` is AMR-scope and this is a Forklift AGV row. Recurring scope asymmetry, 5th+ instance this pass. Also unstorable: 'Over-the-Air-Updates ermöglichen kontinuierliche Produktverbesserungen und die Einführung neuer Features' (factsheet p.2, repeated four times across the factsheet and the flyer) — remote software maintenance is a genuine lifecycle differentiator with no AP0 field; dead weight 650 kg (VDI 2.1.1); sound pressure 54 dB(A) (VDI 10.7) — the quietest vehicle in this corpus and directly relevant to night-shift or office-adjacent operation. PRODUCT-TYPE NOTE: recorded as Forklift AGV (drive_type 'Pallet Mover') to match the DB's existing treatment of the ERE 225a, another Jungheinrich low-lift fork truck. Jungheinrich itself calls it a 'Mobile Robot', which in AP0 vocabulary would suggest Mobile AMR — but it carries forks and lifts a pallet, so Forklift AGV is the better fit. Flagged in case a reviewer disagrees.

autonomous_obstacle_bypass.note: SCORING field. The parenthetical is explicit and appears only on the arculee M — the newer EAE 212a factsheet presents autonomous obstacle avoidance as a headline standard feature ('Der Mobile Robot erkennt Objekte, umfährt Hindernisse selbstständig und sicher'). products.notes: Also documented and worth a reviewer's attention: p.2 'Kompakte Bauweise **im Rotationsradius einer Europalette**' — the vehicle's swept circle is no larger than a Euro pallet's, which is a footprint claim expressed as a rotation radius but with no number attached, so nothing was written to `min_turning_radius` (the DB row stores vehicle_length 1200 × vehicle_width 750, whose circumscribed-circle radius is √(1200²+750²)/2 ≈ 708 mm — consistent with the claim, but derived, not printed). p.2 'Intelligente Personen- und Transportsicherheit, **TÜV-zertifiziert**' — a third-party certification with no AP0 allowed value (`safety_standard` has no TÜV entry, `certifications_generic` has no TÜV entry; the same non-conforming 'TÜV' string already observed on the Kivnon rows). p.2 '360°-Sicherheitssensorik … zur Überwachung der Gesamtkontur' — angular coverage again, so `safety_coverage` left null. p.2 'Lasthöhe 2,1 m' — the maximum height of the load the robot can carry underneath itself, which is neither `lift_height` (the jack stroke) nor `min_ground_clearance` (the robot's own height, already 290 in the DB); AP0 has no field for the carried load's height envelope. **New gap, and a real one for underride AMRs.** `navigation_type`: p.3 'Kombination aus kontur- und markerbasierter Navigation passend für jeden Einsatz' — consistent with the DB's existing SLAM|QR|Reflector triple; p.2 'markerfreie Navigation'. `battery_type` Li-Ion confirmed ('leistungsstarker Lithium-Ionen-Technologie … kann er schnell zwischengeladen werden', p.2). `workflow_capability`: the DB holds 'Transport|Goods-to-Person'; this factsheet describes only transport plus 'Bereitstellung auf Übergabestationen in ergonomischer Arbeitshöhe' (p.3) — which is presentation at an ergonomic height, arguably G2P-adjacent. Not changed. products.notes: The datasheet CONFIRMS the DB row on every K.O. field: max_payload=1500 (p.1 and VDI 1.5), lifting_height=6000 (p.1 'Hubhöhe: 2750-6000 mm'; p.3 mast table's top ZT option, h3 6000 / h1 3890 / h4 6885), min_aisle_width=3300 (p.4 VDI row '4.34.2 Arbeitsgangbreite (Palette 800x1200 längs) Ast mm 3300'), min_total_height=2730 (p.4 VDI row '4.2.1 Gesamthöhe h15 mm 2730'), max_speed=1.95 (p.4 row '5.1 Fahrgeschwindigkeit mit/ohne Last km/h 5 / 7' → 7 ÷ 3.6 = 1.94; the DB's 1.95 is the same figure rounded up). **A caveat the DB structurally cannot hold, and it matters:** the whole VDI table is footnoted 'Die Werte in der Tabelle gelten für Hubgerüst **ZT3500 mm**' — so the stored min_aisle_width (3300), min_total_height (2730) and axle loads all belong to the 3500 mm mast, while the stored lifting_height (6000) belongs to the tallest mast. For the 6000 mm mast, p.3 gives h1 = 3890 mm, i.e. the true lowered height of the machine the row claims to describe is **1160 mm taller than the stored min_total_height**. A doorway-height K.O. would pass this configuration wrongly. This is the same 'one row, several mast configurations' problem seen on the STILL FM-X and Linde R-MATIC k, but here it produces an internally inconsistent row rather than merely an imprecise one. **Recommend the reviewer either pin the row to one mast option or split it.** BATTERY — the worked false-positive example: VDI rows 6.3/6.4 say '5 PzS 775' and '24 / 775 V/Ah' (lead-acid), the DB says Li-Ion, and the companion `eks-215a-2021-factsheet…pdf` says 'Das 24-V-Energiekonzept mit **Lithium-Ionen-Batterie** und Automatik-Ladefunktion'. No conflict; the DB is right. Other factsheet support for existing values: safety_standard/`safety_coverage` — 'Serienmäßige Personenschutzscanner scannen …', 'Smartes Sicherheitskonzept mit integrierte[n] Sicherheitssensoren [an den] Gabeln', 'Optionale Scanner oder Warnfelder'; navigation_type='Laser Reflector' — 'Präzise Lasernavigation mittels [Reflektoren]'; station_applications — 'nicht unterfahrbare Stationen sowie die Abgabe in Regalen'. Unstorable: fork spread is adjustable on a fixed raster, p.5 footnote 'VDI-Nr. 4.2.5: Gabelaußenabstand einstellbar im Raster: 336 / 412 / 488 / 565 / 641 / 717 / 793 / 856 mm' — eight discrete positions, which `fork_spread`'s ['None','Manual','Auto'] cannot express (4th instance of that gap this pass); direction-dependent speed, p.5 footnote 'VDI-Nr. 5.1: Geschwindigkeit in Lastrichtung: 4,3 km/h' (1.19 m/s, less than two thirds of the headline); dead weight 3280 kg; sound pressure 65 dB(A).

lifting_height.source: p.3, the ERC 217a mast table lists exactly TWO options — 'Hub (h3) 2840 mm / h1 2150 mm / Freihub 200 mm / h4 3495 mm' and 'Hub (h3) 3540 mm / h1 2500 mm / Freihub 200 mm / h4 4195 mm'. There is no 4400 mm option for the 217a. 4400 mm is the top option in the ERC **213a** table immediately above it on the same page.
lifting_height.note: K.O. field, and a textbook sibling-row error: the ERC 213a's maximum lift has been copied onto the ERC 217a row. The two models are printed one above the other on p.3 with separate tables, which is exactly the layout that produces this mistake. The correct maximum for the 217a is 3540 mm — 860 mm lower. **This is the single most actionable conflict in the Jungheinrich group**: the row currently claims a rack height the truck cannot reach. Payload/height trade-off is the reason: the 217a carries 400 kg more (1700 vs 1300 kg) and gives up lift for it, the same coupling documented on the Linde L-MATIC AC and the Balyo Reach Truck.

min_total_height.note: NOT a conflict as such — 2150 is correct for the shorter mast. Flagged only because it is inconsistent with the row's (incorrect) stored lifting_height: if the row is meant to describe the tallest 217a build, min_total_height should be 2500.

lifting_height.source: p.6–p.7 mast tables. There are four, and each names the models it applies to: (1) 'EKX 514a, EKX 516ka, EKX 516a' — DZ 4000–9500 mm and ZT 3000–9500 mm; (2) '**EKX 516a**' — DZ 11000–14500 mm; (3) 'EKX 516ka, EKX 516a' — DZ 10000–10500 mm and ZT 10000–10500 mm. **The EKX 514a appears only in table (1), whose ceiling is 9500 mm.**
lifting_height.note: K.O. field. The DB claims 13 000 mm for a model whose own mast programme stops at 9500 mm — a 3.5 m overstatement on the field that decides high-bay tenders. The 13 000 figure is inside the EKX **516a**'s range (table 2), so this looks like the same sibling-copy error as the ERC 217a, from a document whose tables are deliberately model-scoped. CAVEAT — the document is not perfectly self-consistent: p.1's header reads 'EKX 5a / Hubhöhe: **11000-13000 mm** / Tragfähigkeit: 1400-1600 kg', a family-level range that only the 516a can actually deliver. So a reader taking the front page at face value would arrive at exactly the DB's number. Flagged, not resolved — worth a direct question to Jungheinrich.

products.notes: CONFIRMS max_payload=1400 (p.8, VDI row '1.5 Tragfähigkeit/Last Q kg **1400** | 1600' — the 514a column), vehicle_length=3665 (VDI row 4.19, first column), max_speed=2.92 (VDI row '5.1 Fahrgeschwindigkeit mit/ohne Last km/h **10,5 / 10,5** | 12 / 12' → 10.5 ÷ 3.6 = 2.92), mast_type='Triplex' (p.6 'Dreifach-Hubgerüst DZ'), guidance='Wire' and busbar_compatible=1 (factsheet: 'Stromschiene und -abnehmer … bestens gerüstet für den 24/7-Einsatz'). All three EKX vehicle_length values in the DB (3665 / 3775 / 4045) match VDI row 4.19 exactly — this part of the record was built carefully, which makes the lift-height errors look like an isolated mistake rather than a sloppy row. min_aisle_width=1727 is NOT stated anywhere in these two files (the Typenblatt has no row 4.34) — neither confirmed nor contradicted; left alone. Dead weight 6350 kg. Seat height 430 mm (VDI 4.8) — a MAN-UP truck, which AP0 cannot distinguish from man-down though it changes the safety case (2nd instance this session, after Linde K-MATIC). Battery 3 PzS 465 at 80 V (VDI 6.3/6.4) — lead-acid on the Typenblatt, and the DB's 'Lead-Acid|Li-Ion' is consistent. VDI row 6.6 'Energieverbrauch nach VDI-Zyklus kWh/h **0**' is evidently a placeholder, not a measurement — row 6.6.1 gives the real figure, 4,94 kWh/h nach EN-Zyklus, and 6.6.2 gives 2,67 kg/h CO₂ equivalent per EN ISO 23308. Worth noting as a source-side data-quality artefact of the kind that can poison an automated extraction.
